  {"id": 4, "label": "polychronic (from Edward Hall)", "description": "This means doing many things at once, putting people and the business at hand before a preset schedule, seldom feeling that time is wasted, and hearing people out, schedule or no schedule."},
  {"id": 5, "label": "self-starting", "description": "This means taking up the dreaded task today, before anything else and with no one pushing, and getting going long before the deadline comes near."},
  {"id": 6, "label": "efficient", "description": "This means getting the job done right with the least time and effort: the shortest route, no step taken twice, and stopping the moment it is finished."},
  {"id": 7, "label": "inefficient", "description": "This means being wasteful of time and effort: the long way around, the job done twice, extra steps that serve nothing, and never a thought for the hours."},
  {"id": 8, "label": "monochronic (from Edward Hall)", "description": "This means doing one thing at a time, organizing life around tasks, schedules and procedures, treating time as a thing to be saved, spent, wasted or lost, and keeping to the clock."},
  {"id": 9, "label": "learning-oriented", "description": "This means doing each task to get better at it, taking the hard problem over the sure win, and judging it by what one learned."},
  {"id": 10, "label": "unhurried", "description": "This means being in no hurry about anything, treating nothing as pressing, letting things wait until convenient, and assuming that whatever it is will keep."},
  {"id": 11, "label": "performance-oriented", "description": "This means doing each task to show how good one is, taking the sure win over the hard problem, and judging it by the score, not by what one learned."},
  {"id": 12, "label": "competent", "description": "This means knowing how to do the job and getting it right, handling the task in front of one with sure hands, and turning out work that holds up."},
  {"id": 13, "label": "distractible", "description": "This means having one's attention pulled off the task by every buzz, noise or passing thought, drifting mid-sentence and losing the thread."},

  {"id": 15, "label": "incompetent", "description": "This means not knowing how to do the job and getting it wrong despite trying, fumbling the task in front of one, and turning out work that falls apart."},
  {"id": 16, "label": "strategic", "description": "This means taking each problem as one piece of a larger plan, passing up the move that wins now for the one that wins in the end, looking at the large-scale picture and the long game, and always keeping a fallback."}
